parts.title: Word List 1
parts.content:
Word List 1

Detailed Meanings

😎
temptation[tempˈteɪʃn]n.
a desire to do something, especially something wrong or unwise. (sự cám dỗ, sự quyến rũ)
→ He felt the temptation to eat the whole cake. (Anh ấy cảm thấy sự cám dỗ muốn ăn hết cả cái bánh.)
😎
if only[ɪf ˈoʊnli]phrase
used to express a wish. (giá mà)
→ If only fast food were truly addictive. (Giá như thức ăn nhanh thực sự gây nghiện.)
😎
fast food[fæst fuːd]n.
food that can be prepared quickly and easily. (thức ăn nhanh)
→ She eats too much fast food. (Cô ấy ăn quá nhiều thức ăn nhanh.)
😎
addictive[əˈdɪktɪv]adj.
causing or likely to cause an addiction. (nghiện, hấp dẫn)
→ Nicotine is a highly addictive substance. (Nicotine là một chất gây nghiện rất cao.)
😎
file[faɪl]v.
to submit (a legal document, application, or charge) to be placed on record. (nộp, đưa (đơn))
→ He filed a lawsuit against the company. (Anh ta đã đệ đơn kiện công ty.)
😎
class-action[klæs ˈækʃn]n.
a lawsuit filed or defended by an individual acting on behalf of a group. (tập thể)
→ They filed a class-action lawsuit. (Họ đã đệ đơn kiện tập thể.)
😎
lawsuit[ˈlɔːsuːt]n.
a claim or dispute brought to a court of law. (việc kiện cáo, việc tố tụng)
→ The absurd lawsuit may have been inevitable. (Vụ kiện vô lý có thể là không thể tránh khỏi.)
😎
claim[kleɪm]n.
a demand or request for something considered one's due. (sự đòi, sự yêu sách)
→ His claim was that they were responsible. (Yêu sách của anh ta là họ phải chịu trách nhiệm.)
😎
obesity[oʊˈbiːsəti]n.
the condition of being grossly fat or overweight. (sự béo phì)
→ Obesity is a major health problem. (Béo phì là một vấn đề sức khỏe lớn.)
😎
craving[ˈkreɪvɪŋ]n.
a powerful desire for something. (sự thèm muốn, lòng khao khát)
→ Fast food had created a craving in his client. (Thức ăn nhanh đã tạo ra một sự thèm muốn ở thân chủ của ông ấy.)
😎
hapless[ˈhæpləs]adj.
unfortunate. (rủi ro, không may)
→ The hapless victim was completely unaware. (Nạn nhân kém may mắn hoàn toàn không biết gì.)
😎
client[ˈklaɪənt]n.
a person using the services of a professional person or organization. (khách hàng, thân chủ)
→ The lawyer represented his client well. (Luật sư đã đại diện tốt cho thân chủ của mình.)
😎
blissfully[ˈblɪsfəli]adv.
in a manner characterized by extreme happiness or joy. (hạnh phúc, sung sướng)
→ He was blissfully unaware of the danger. (Anh ta sung sướng không hề biết về mối nguy hiểm.)
😎
unaware[ˌʌnəˈwer]adj.
having no knowledge of a situation or fact. (không biết, không hay)
→ She was completely unaware of the changes. (Cô ấy hoàn toàn không hay biết về những thay đổi.)
😎
consume[kənˈsuːm]v.
to eat, drink, or ingest. (dùng, tiêu thụ)
→ Consuming huge piles of burgers is not healthy. (Tiêu thụ một đống lớn bánh mì kẹp thịt thì không tốt cho sức khỏe.)
😎
absurd[əbˈsɜːrd]adj.
wildly unreasonable, illogical, or inappropriate. (vô lý, lố bịch)
→ It was an absurd lawsuit. (Đó là một vụ kiện lố bịch.)
😎
inevitable[ɪnˈevɪtəbl]adj.
certain to happen; unavoidable. (tất yếu, không thể tránh được)
→ The accident was inevitable. (Vụ tai nạn là không thể tránh khỏi.)
😎
settlement[ˈsetlmənt]n.
an official agreement intended to resolve a dispute or conflict. (sự dàn xếp, sự hòa giải)
→ They reached a settlement out of court. (Họ đã đạt được một thỏa thuận hòa giải ngoài tòa án.)
😎
catch[kætʃ]n.
a hidden problem or disadvantage in an apparently ideal situation. (điều bất lợi)
→ There is a catch: fast food is not addictive. (Có một điều bất lợi: thức ăn nhanh không gây nghiện.)
😎
as a matter of fact[əz ə ˈmætər əv fækt]phrase
in reality; actually. (vì vậy, thực tế là)
→ As a matter of fact, I do know him. (Thực tế là tôi có biết anh ta.)
😎
contain[kənˈteɪn]v.
to have or hold within. (chứa, đựng)
→ The box contains some old books. (Chiếc hộp chứa một vài cuốn sách cũ.)
😎
substance[ˈsʌbstəns]n.
a particular kind of matter with uniform properties. (chất)
→ It contains no addictive substance. (Nó không chứa bất kỳ chất gây nghiện nào.)
😎
induce[ɪnˈduːs]v.
to succeed in persuading or influencing someone to do something. (gây ra, đem lại)
→ Nothing could induce me to change my mind. (Không gì có thể thuyết phục tôi thay đổi ý định.)
😎
plight[plaɪt]n.
a dangerous, difficult, or otherwise unfortunate situation. (hoàn cảnh, cảnh ngộ)
→ Consider the plight of the poor plaintiffs. (Hãy xem xét hoàn cảnh của những nguyên đơn nghèo khổ.)
😎
plaintiff[ˈpleɪntɪf]n.
a person who brings a case against another in a court of law. (nguyên đơn, người đứng đơn kiện)
→ The plaintiff won the lawsuit. (Nguyên đơn đã thắng kiện.)
😎
compel[kəmˈpel]v.
to force or oblige someone to do something. (buộc phải, bắt buộc)
→ They were physiologically compelled to consume fast food. (Họ bị ép buộc về mặt sinh lý phải tiêu thụ đồ ăn nhanh.)
😎
common sense[ˌkɑːmən ˈsens]n.
good sense and sound judgment in practical matters. (lẽ thường)
→ Use your common sense. (Hãy sử dụng lẽ thường của bạn.)
😎
indulge in[ɪnˈdʌldʒ ɪn]phrasal v.
to allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of. (ham mê, say mê)
→ Millions more indulge in the stuff. (Hàng triệu người khác say mê thứ đó.)
😎
suborn[səˈbɔːrn]v.
to bribe or otherwise induce someone to commit an unlawful act. (hối lộ, mua chuộc)
→ They knew they had been suborned into doing so. (Họ biết rằng mình đã bị mua chuộc để làm như vậy.)

sections.title: Exercise 1: Choose the correct word to fill in the blank.

questions.content: I tried to resist the ________ to laugh.
questions.explanation: Temptation means a desire to do something, especially something wrong or unwise.

questions.content: They ________ an application to have their case heard early.
questions.explanation: File means to submit a legal document to be placed on record.

questions.content: A confrontation was ________ because they disliked each other so much.
questions.explanation: Inevitable means certain to happen; unavoidable.

questions.content: Heroin is an illegal ________.
questions.explanation: Substance means a particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

questions.content: ________, I do know him.
questions.explanation: As a matter of fact means in reality; actually.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Choose the word that best matches the definition.

questions.content: The condition of being grossly fat or overweight
questions.explanation: Obesity is the condition of being grossly fat or overweight.

questions.content: A person who brings a case against another in a court of law
questions.explanation: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

questions.content: To force or oblige someone to do something
questions.explanation: Compel means to force or oblige someone to do something.

sections.title: Exercise 3: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: A 'class-action' lawsuit is filed by one person on behalf of a group.
questions.explanation: True. A class-action lawsuit is filed or defended by an individual acting on behalf of a group.

questions.content: If someone is 'blissfully unaware', they know exactly what is happening.
questions.explanation: False. Blissfully unaware means having no knowledge of a situation, while feeling happy.

questions.content: To 'indulge in' something means to allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of it.
questions.explanation: True. Indulge in means to allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of something.

parts.title: Word List 2
parts.content:
Word List 2

Detailed Meanings

😎
genuine[ˈdʒenjuɪn]adj.
truly what something is said to be; authentic. (thật, chính xác, thành thật)
→ Once fast food became a genuine compulsion. (Một khi thức ăn nhanh trở thành một sự ép buộc thực sự.)
😎
compulsion[kəmˈpʌlʃn]n.
an irresistible urge to behave in a certain way. (sự ép buộc, sự cưỡng bức)
→ Eating disorder is a compulsion. (Rối loạn ăn uống là một sự cưỡng bức.)
😎
objection[əbˈdʒekʃn]n.
an expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition. (sự phản đối, sự chống đối)
→ There could be no economic or moral objection. (Không thể có sự phản đối nào về mặt kinh tế hay đạo đức.)
😎
regulate[ˈreɡjuleɪt]v.
to control or maintain the rate or speed of (a machine or process). (quy định)
→ Alcohol and tobacco are regulated. (Rượu và thuốc lá đều bị quy định chặt chẽ.)
😎
consumption[kənˈsʌmpʃn]n.
the using up of a resource. (sự tiêu thụ)
→ Regulating its consumption. (Quy định việc tiêu thụ nó.)
😎
revenue[ˈrevənuː]n.
income, especially when of a company or organization. (thu nhập)
→ The revenue from this tax could be used. (Doanh thu từ khoản thuế này có thể được sử dụng.)
😎
sin tax[sɪn tæks]n.
a tax on items considered undesirable or harmful, such as alcohol or tobacco. (thuế đánh vào những sản phẩm có thể gây hại như rượu bia, thuốc lá)
→ A sin tax on fast food. (Thuế tội lỗi đối với thức ăn nhanh.)
😎
wean off[wiːn ɔːf]phrasal v.
to make someone gradually stop doing or using something. (bỏ, cai)
→ To wean people off bad food. (Để cai nghiện thức ăn không lành mạnh cho mọi người.)
😎
balance[ˈbæləns]v.
to keep or put (something) in a steady position. (cân đối)
→ On balancing budgets. (Trong việc cân đối ngân sách.)
😎
budget[ˈbʌdʒɪt]n.
an estimate of income and expenditure for a set period of time. (ngân sách)
→ The school has a strict budget. (Trường có một ngân sách nghiêm ngặt.)
😎
prudent[ˈpruːdnt]adj.
acting with or showing care and thought for the future. (thận trọng, khôn ngoan)
→ It is prudent to save money. (Việc tiết kiệm tiền là rất khôn ngoan.)
😎
defendant[dɪˈfendənt]n.
an individual, company, or institution sued or accused in a court of law. (bị cáo)
→ Making fast food addictive could help the defendants as well. (Làm cho thức ăn nhanh gây nghiện cũng có thể giúp ích cho các bị cáo.)
😎
living proof[ˈlɪvɪŋ pruːf]n.
a person who provides an example of something. (bằng chứng sống)
→ Tobacco firms are living proof of this. (Các hãng thuốc lá là một bằng chứng sống cho điều này.)
😎
murderous[ˈmɜːrdərəs]adj.
capable of or intending to murder; dangerously violent. (giết người, tàn sát)
→ Even after murderous litigation. (Ngay cả sau vụ kiện tàn sát.)
😎
litigation[ˌlɪtɪˈɡeɪʃn]n.
the process of taking legal action. (sự kiện tụng, sự tranh chấp)
→ The company faces costly litigation. (Công ty phải đối mặt với vụ kiện tốn kém.)
😎
universally[ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːrsəli]adv.
by everyone; in every case. (khắp nơi, phổ biến)
→ You can be universally reviled and still successful. (Bạn có thể bị cả thế giới chửi rủa mà vẫn thành công.)
😎
revile[rɪˈvaɪl]v.
to criticize in an abusive or angrily insulting manner. (chửi mắng, xỉ vả)
→ The politician was reviled by the press. (Chính trị gia đó đã bị báo chí xỉ vả.)
😎
nigh[naɪ]adj.
near. (sớm (xảy ra))
→ Some thought the end of the industry was nigh. (Một số người nghĩ rằng ngày tàn của ngành công nghiệp này sắp đến.)
😎
far from[fɑːr frəm]phrase
not at all. (không hề, hầu như là trái lại)
→ Far from it. (Hoàn toàn không phải vậy.)
😎
fiddly[ˈfɪdli]adj.
complicated or detailed and awkward to do or use. (vớ vẩn, vô nghĩa)
→ Fiddly rules about not marketing to small children. (Những quy định vớ vẩn về việc không tiếp thị cho trẻ nhỏ.)
😎
firm[fɜːrm]n.
a business or company. (hãng sản xuất)
→ Cigarette firms can still earn money. (Các hãng thuốc lá vẫn có thể kiếm được tiền.)
😎
follow suit[ˈfɑːloʊ suːt]idiom
to conform to another's actions. (làm theo như vậy)
→ Fast-food companies could follow suit. (Các công ty thức ăn nhanh có thể sẽ làm theo như vậy.)
😎
reap[riːp]v.
to receive (a reward or benefit) as a consequence of one's own or other people's actions. (gặt hái, thu hoạch, hưởng)
→ They reap both public-relations and financial victories. (Họ gặt hái cả chiến thắng về mặt quan hệ công chúng lẫn tài chính.)
😎
financial[faɪˈnænʃl]adj.
relating to finance or finances. (thuộc tài chính)
→ Financial victories. (Chiến thắng về tài chính.)
😎
stockmarket[ˈstɑːkmɑːrkɪt]n.
a stock exchange. (thị trường chứng khoán)
→ Theirs was the best-performing industry in the stockmarket. (Của họ là ngành hoạt động tốt nhất trên thị trường chứng khoán.)

questions.content: An irresistible urge to behave in a certain way
questions.explanation: Compulsion is an irresistible urge to behave in a certain way.

questions.content: To receive a reward or benefit as a consequence of actions
questions.explanation: Reap means to receive a reward or benefit as a consequence of actions.

questions.content: Truly what something is said to be; authentic
questions.explanation: Genuine means truly what something is said to be; authentic.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
Comprehensive Reading

Oh, Temptation

If only fast food were truly addictive.

Last week, Caesar Barber of New York filed a class-action lawsuit against McDonald's, Kentucky Fried Chicken, Burger King and Wendy's, four of the world's biggest fast-food chains. His claim was that they were responsible for his obesity and poor health. According to his lawyer, fast food had created a "craving" in his hapless client, who was blissfully unaware, until his doctor told him, that consuming huge piles of burgers, fries and milkshakes was not actually good for his health.

Such an absurd lawsuit may have been inevitable as soon as the big tobacco settlements began burning a hole in trial lawyers' pockets. But there is a catch: fast food is not addictive. It does not, as a matter of fact, create a real physical craving, because it contains no substance that could induce one.

The Economist suggests that this should now change. Consider the plight of the poor plaintiffs. They must prove that they were physiologically compelled to consume fast food, against the weight of scientific evidence and the dictates of common sense. Then there are the millions more who indulge in the stuff, but who would feel much better about themselves if they knew they had been suborned into doing so. Through the simple introduction of minute amounts of cocaine or nicotine into their wares, fast-food companies could improve the lot of such folk in future.

The benefits would not stop there. Nobody should be keener for fast food to be made addictive than governments. Once fast food became a genuine compulsion, there could be no economic or moral objection to regulating its consumption, as alcohol and tobacco are regulated, and to taxing it. The revenue from this "sin tax" could be used in a pretend effort to wean people off bad food. Many states spent their millions from tobacco settlements on balancing budgets, improving roads or paying teachers more. Supposedly, people in fiscally prudent, literate and well-paved places felt less urge to light up.

Making fast food addictive could help the defendants as well. They might follow the tobacco firms, who are living proof that even after murderous litigation you can be both universally reviled and still successful. When the big tobacco lawsuits finished, some thought the end of the industry was nigh. Far from it: they may have to obey fiddly rules about not marketing to small children in North America, but cigarette firms can still earn money in the rest of the world. Last year, theirs was the best-performing industry in the stockmarket. Fast-food companies could follow suit and reap both public-relations and financial victories.

sections.title: Exercise 1: Fill in each blank with the appropriate word
sections.content: Drag and drop the correct words into the blanks.

questions.content:
1. If only fast food were truly [ 1 ].

2. Caesar Barber filed a [ 2 ] lawsuit against fast-food chains.

3. His claim was that they were responsible for his [ 3 ].

4. Fast food had created a "[ 4 ]" in his hapless client.

5. Such an absurd lawsuit may have been [ 5 ].

6. It contains no [ 6 ] that could induce a craving.

7. Consider the plight of the poor [ 7 ].

8. They must prove that they were physiologically [ 8 ] to consume fast food.

9. Once fast food became a [ 9 ] compulsion...

10. There could be no objection to [ 10 ] its consumption.

11. Fast-food companies could [ 11 ] and reap financial victories.
What was Caesar Barber's main claim in the lawsuit?
options: Fast-food chains used illegal substances in their food.
Fast-food chains were responsible for his obesity and poor health.
Fast-food chains refused to serve him.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'His claim was that they were responsible for his obesity and poor health.'

questions.content: According to the passage, why is the lawsuit considered 'absurd'?
options: Because the plaintiff was not really obese.
Because fast food is not actually addictive and contains no addictive substance.
Because the fast-food chains had already settled.
Because the judge dismissed the case immediately.
questions.explanation: The text says: 'fast food is not addictive. It does not, as a matter of fact, create a real physical craving, because it contains no substance that could induce one.'

questions.content: What satirical suggestion does The Economist make?
options: Fast-food companies should lower their prices.
Fast-food companies should add addictive substances to their food.
Fast-food companies should close their restaurants.
Fast-food companies should only serve healthy food.
questions.explanation: The text satirically suggests: 'Through the simple introduction of minute amounts of cocaine or nicotine into their wares, fast-food companies could improve the lot of such folk.'

questions.content: What does the passage say about tobacco companies after major lawsuits?
options: They were universally reviled but still successful.
questions.explanation: The text states: tobacco firms 'are living proof that even after murderous litigation you can be both universally reviled and still successful.'
